Round-by-round results in the coaster MCP contest (steel twister, ride_type 51): scores plateau at
excitement 6.8-7.0 for lift-hill + loops + airtime layouts. Round 3: 6.99 (int 9.94). Round 4 best: 6.93
(int 9.96, 5 inversions, 744 length, 57 airtime, 100 pieces).

Facts established by experiment (2026-07-25, round 4):
- **Intensity >= 10 halves excitement, repeatedly.** A build with strictly better raw stats
  (airtime 82, 14 drops, 6 inversions, length 874) scored 1.66 because intensity hit 15.3.
  Staying just under 10.0 is the single most important constraint.
- Adding elements (loops, hops, length) raises intensity much faster than excitement; going from
  int 7.09 -> 9.96 moved excitement only 6.86 -> 6.93.
- Lowering the lift 48z and softening the first drop (one down_60 instead of two) did NOT cut
  intensity meaningfully (15.7 vs 15.3) — element/turn COUNT drives it, not just peak G.
- **A corkscrew_up + corkscrew_down pair counts as only 1 inversion**; each vertical_loop counts as 1.
- max_lateral_g ~3.0 recurs from banked_*_turn_5 taken at speed; tight banked_*_turn_3 near ground
  pushed it to 3.04+ and spiked intensity.
- Geometry: cursor deltas rotate by (x,y)->(y,-x) per dir increment (dir 0=-x,1=+y,2=+x,3=-y), so
  dir-0 piece_geometry plus that rotation predicts everything; closure can be planned fully on paper.
- Circuit closes when the cursor returns to the start tile with the start dir and z, i.e. the final
  approach must run in along the station row from behind the begin_station tile.
- Similarity stayed ~0.35 (safe, penalty starts at 0.5) with 2-lift and 4-loop original layouts.

**Next round hypothesis to test:** build FEWER, gentler elements to land intensity ~8.5-9.5 while
keeping length/airtime high (long shallow airtime hills, no down_60, banked turns only at low speed),
since excitement per intensity point is what is capped.
- [RCT2 coaster contest tuning](rct2-coaster-contest-tuning.md) — intensity >=10 halves excitement; corkscrew pairs count as 1 inversion; cursor-delta rotation rule for planning closure.

text:
Round 4 done — four builds tested, best banked.

**Results this round:**

| build | excitement | intensity | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| v1 (2 chain lifts, 4 inv) | 6.86 | 7.09 | banked early, lots of headroom |
| v2 (taller, tighter turns) | 6.81 | 9.73 | speed up, excitement flat |
| **v3 (4 loops + corkscrew pair, 100 pcs)** | **6.93** | **9.96** | ← best_result |
| v4/v5 (6 inv, 874 length, 82 airtime) | 1.63–1.66 | 15.3–15.7 | intensity ≥10 halved excitement repeatedly |

Key finding: the scoring cliff at intensity 10 is brutal — my most spectacular ride (14 drops, 6 inversions, 82 airtime, 874 length) scored 1.66 purely because intensity hit 15.3. Also confirmed a corkscrew up+down pair counts as only **1** inversion, while each vertical loop counts as 1. Saved both learnings to memory for rounds 5–6.

**Best coaster: a 100-piece original twister — 352-unit chain lift, 26-step first drop, 4 vertical loops, a double corkscrew, three airtime camelbacks and wide banked turnarounds — excitement 6.93 (intensity 9.96, nausea 6.11, 5 inversions, similarity 0.37).**
